content:
anya: Heads-up — seeing a ~30-40% drop in NCCL allreduce throughput across a subset of euc1 racks since the infra patch last night (OFED 5.4.2 -> 5.5.0 + NIC FW 3.7.1). Affected jobs are mostly rex-* tenants. :rotating_light:

tim: :eyes: which nodes/racks? can you paste the quick repro/logs?

anya: Quick summary logs from one affected host (r-euc1-32):
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v | egrep 'device | fw_ver'
device: mlx5_core 0
fw_ver: 3.7.1

$ dmesg | tail -n 20 | egrep 'mlx5|ib|NCCL'
[ 4621.123] mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: EQ overflow, drop event
[ 4621.124] mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: NIC hw err, resetting
[ 4621.200] nv_peer_mem: nv_p2p: peer not supported by device
[ 4621.455] NCCL WARN Transport mlx5 failed, falling back to Socket (TCP)
```

kyle: that EQ overflow + reset pattern smells like FW/driver timing regression. we saw similar on a couple of test nodes with 3.7.x last year. not all hosts have it though — config mismatch likely.

sophie: do we have which kernel + MLX modules these have? could be module ABI break vs kernel.

anya: kernel is 5.15.0-1013 on these hosts. modinfo mlx5_core shows src version matching our build pipeline. But OFED package set updated pointers to newer mlx5 driver in the package.

raj: short mitigation: we can force jobs to use socket transport (NCCL IB disabled) until we fix infra. set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 in the job wrapper or ML platform env. not ideal for perf but buys time.

tim: agree. also need to mark affected nodes in autoscaler so scheduler doesn't assign critical low-latency jobs.

anya: I've run a grep across infra metrics to identify nodes with increased socket fallback rate. list of ~18 nodes across racks r-euc1-[30..35] and r-euc1-[40..42].

infra-bot: Deploy note: OFED 5.5.0 + NIC-FW 3.7.1 rolled to euc1 at 02:10 UTC via canary->region rollout. Canary cluster showed no immediate errors.

kyle: plan proposal: 1) pin new jobs in affected nodes to NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, 2) schedule 10-node firmware rollback (3.7.1 -> 3.7.0) as a canary tonight, 3) if rollback clears EQ resets, roll back region, else escalate to vendor/driver debug.

sophie: +1. also capture per-node ethtool/ib counters before rollback: `ethtool -S mlx5_core` and `perf record -a` on a repro job. we should collect mlx5 logs and open a bug with vendor with those artifacts.

raj: cost note: forcing sockets will increase token-cost by ~25-50% on those runs due to higher CPU usage + latency. recommend moving non-urgent training batches to other regions (us-west/eu-central) for the next 24–48h. ops: can we toggle autoscaler to prefer non-euc1 zones?

tim: ops — yes, will add a soft placement rule to avoid euc1 for new preemptible/spot pools.

anya: quick commands to triage/identify affected nodes (run as root):
```
sudo dmesg | egrep "mlx5|EQ overflow|NIC hw err"
sudo ibv_devinfo -v | egrep "fw_ver|device"
sudo ethtool -S <mlx_iface> | egrep "tx_bytes|rx_bytes|eq_overflow"
```

kyle: one more note — if kernel ABI mismatch is the root, rollback might not help. we should also check our internal driver build job that packages mlx5 against kernel-headers. check build id: redwood-mlx5-20260316-57.

anya: opened a short incident doc and linked the artifact bucket: gs://redwood-logs/euc1/1710609876/ — collecting perf traces and dmesg dumps now. I've tagged the affected nodes in CMDB with label `nccl-degraded=2026-03-18`.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2289 — Priority: P2. Owner: kyle. Runbook step 2 scheduled: nightly rollback window 02:00-03:30 UTC pending approval.

sophie: kyle can you own the rollback canary? I'll prepare the telemetry and vendor ticket if canary shows same pattern.

kyle: will own. timeline: will pick 10 nodes (from your list) at 02:00, rollback NIC FW to 3.7.0, monitor NCCL transport and CX counters for 30m. if clears, escalate rollback for remaining affected racks.

tim: fine, ops will pause any infra upgrades for other regions until we have vendor sign-off. also will post a notice in #announcements to flag ongoing impact for teams.

anya: thanks all — for immediate action I pushed a small config to platform to set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for new rex-* jobs in euc1. will update as canary feedback arrives. :thumbsup:

raj: FYI running a quick script to migrate low-priority queued jobs away from euc1. will report counts shortly.

anya: last note — if you have any long-running experiments in euc1, please checkpoint and/or pause until we stabilize.

kyle: logged vendor ticket with Mellanox support (case 987654). attaching dmesg + ethtool dumps. vendor acknowledged EQ overflow signature and requested perf traces.

sophie: good. keep this thread updated with canary outcome.

anya: will do. updating incident doc with every major step.
